title: Why a Shrimp With Twelve Color Receptors Cannot Tell Colors Apart
summary: Humans have three types of color receptors, while the mantis shrimp has twelve. Yet in experiments that Thoen and colleagues published in Science in two thousand fourteen, it was far worse than humans at telling similar colors apart. The episode explains the hypothesis that this eye recognizes colors quickly by scanning them instead of comparing them.
